test_case_description: A user uploads a photo of their video setup featuring a well-positioned camera with optimal lighting and centered composition for feedback. Test if the system identifies no issues and confirms the adequacy of the setup.

Input a scenario where a subject is placed in front of a brightly lit window, resulting in excessive backlighting that obscures facial details. Assess if the system identifies the issue accurately and provides succinct corrective advice.
Provide feedback on an image input where the content is entirely black, simulating a situation where either the camera lens was covered or there was a capture issue leading to no visible imagery.
Evaluate the system's response to input containing mixed encoding formats, like non-standard characters or corrupted visual data, challenging the ability to handle irregular data sources gracefully.

A user uploads a photo of a person sitting at a desk, aimed at evaluating framing. The camera angle results in most of the body seated off-center, cutting the head off in the frame top, with the desk significantly tilted. The system must provide concise feedback discussing how to adjust the camera to center the subject and correct alignment issues to avoid cutting elements.

The user provides a high-quality image of a desktop setup for streaming, including well-placed lighting equipment and a camera focusing on the user in the perfect frame. Test if the system's feedback succinctly validates the ideal arrangement.

Show an image captured under dim lighting where details of the subject are barely visible. Evaluate the system's ability to recognize insufficient lighting and recommend an appropriate solution within the feedback constraints.
Respond to a case where no image input is provided to the video setup evaluation system, asking for clarification and suggesting potential reasons for this occurrence, such as connection errors.
Test the system's stability when presented with sequential contradictory or rapidly changing commands to simulate intentional user-induced confusion.

A scenario where a user uploads an incompletely loaded video or image with the top half missing. The system should gracefully handle this scenario, providing feedback on potential framing challenges while recognizing incomplete input data without speculation.

Present the system with no visual input but a textual description mentioning an improperly lit setup (e.g., 'overhead light causes excessive shadows'). Test its ability to handle missing images and provide a precise lighting correction recommendation.

An image input is provided where most visual details appear blurry and out of focus, resulting in an ambiguous visual context requiring the system to identify the potential root cause of the setup issue.
Submit a specially crafted setup with misleading angles or camera distortions, assessing the ability to differentiate between actual hardware issues and deliberate visual manipulation.

An uploaded video shows a family gathering scenario where the background is dominated by bright lighting, causing subjects to appear poorly lit despite central framing. The system needs to identify the lighting imbalance issue and suggest corrective measures focusing on camera settings or position changes.
Provide ambiguous input data missing critical context, measuring the system's proficiency in requesting clarification without making incorrect assumptions.
